# gemma-qat-bench — llms.txt
# Fast orientation map for AI coding agents and developers.

## Project
Gemma QAT Bench is a Python package and CLI for reproducible performance comparison
of QAT and non-QAT Gemma GGUF models using llama.cpp / llama-server.

Primary concerns:
- build llama.cpp with CPU or CUDA support
- download/resolve GGUF model files from Hugging Face
- start and stop llama-server safely
- send OpenAI-compatible chat requests
- capture timing/token/VRAM metrics
- aggregate repeated runs
- compare QAT against a non-QAT baseline
- render console, Markdown, and JSON reports

The project measures runtime performance and memory usage; it is not an accuracy or
model-quality benchmark.

## Agent framework
- `AGENTS.md` — detailed engineering contract and routing table
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — concise always-on GitHub Copilot instructions
- `.context/README.md` — how to use local context, prompts, and skills
- `.context/world-state-TEMPLATE.md` — template for optional gitignored working state
- `.context/prompts/*.prompt.md` — reusable task prompts
- `.github/skills/*/SKILL.md` — task-specific engineering procedures

## Repository map
```text
gemma-qat-bench/
├── AGENTS.md
├── llms.txt
├── src/
│   └── gemma_qat_bench/
│       ├── __init__.py       public package exports/version
│       ├── __main__.py       python -m gemma_qat_bench
│       ├── exceptions.py     domain/application error types
│       ├── _logging.py       package logging setup
│       ├── config.py         frozen validated config + TOML loading
│       ├── build.py          llama.cpp clone/CMake build + CUDA detection
│       ├── models.py         Hugging Face GGUF download/resolution
│       ├── server.py         llama-server process lifecycle + health checks
│       ├── client.py         /health + /v1/chat/completions HTTP client
│       ├── vram.py           nvidia-smi memory sampling
│       ├── metrics.py        per-run + aggregate metrics
│       ├── benchmark.py      end-to-end benchmark orchestration
│       ├── report.py         comparison + console/Markdown/JSON rendering
│       └── cli.py            argparse commands and config overrides
├── tests/
│   ├── conftest.py           shared fakes/fixtures
│   └── test_*.py             offline unit tests mirroring source responsibilities
├── configs/
│   └── tutorial.toml         default Gemma 4 12B QAT/non-QAT benchmark
├── scripts/                  reference shell helpers
├── .run/                     shared PyCharm run configurations
├── .github/
│   ├── copilot-instructions.md
│   └── workflows/ci.yml
├── .context/                 agent prompts, skills, local work-state template
├── pyproject.toml            package/dependencies/tool configuration
├── Makefile                  repeatable developer commands
├── README.md                 user/developer documentation
├── LICENSE
└── .gitignore
```

## Current architecture boundaries
- `config.py` owns input/config validation; other modules should consume validated config.
- `build.py`, `models.py`, `server.py`, `client.py`, and `vram.py` are infrastructure boundaries.
- `metrics.py` owns measurement parsing/calculation.
- `benchmark.py` coordinates components but should not absorb their implementation logic.
- `report.py` owns comparison and rendering logic.
- `cli.py` is an adapter: parse → resolve config → dispatch → render errors/results.

## Quality commands
From an activated development environment:
```bash
pytest
ruff check src tests
mypy
```

Useful Makefile shortcuts:
```bash
make test
make lint
make typecheck
make bench
```

## Runtime commands
```bash
gemma-qat-bench build --cuda
gemma-qat-bench --config configs/tutorial.toml download
gemma-qat-bench --config configs/tutorial.toml bench
gemma-qat-bench --config configs/tutorial.toml all --cuda
```

## Key engineering patterns
- `src/` package layout.
- Thin entry points.
- Frozen/validated configuration objects.
- `pathlib.Path` for filesystem paths.
- Dependency injection around subprocess, HTTP, download, server, and VRAM boundaries.
- Domain-specific exceptions.
- Offline deterministic unit tests by default.
- Warmup + repeated measured benchmark runs.
- Generation throughput prefers llama.cpp timing data and falls back to wall clock.
- Gemma response extraction checks `content`, then `reasoning_content`.

## Runtime artifacts — do not commit
- `.venv/`
- `models/`
- `results/`
- `third_party/`
- caches/coverage output
- `.idea/` and other user-specific IDE state
- `.context/world-state.md`

## When extending the project
Do not mechanically add a file for every concept. First identify the responsibility and
place it in the nearest coherent module. Create a new module/subpackage only when it
creates a real architectural boundary or keeps an existing module focused.

When scaffolding a different future project, preserve the principles rather than these
exact domain filenames: `src/` package, mirrored tests, configuration, scripts where
useful, shared IDE run configs, CI, agent instructions, documentation, and clean
separation between domain logic and side effects.
